For 21 days after the second report, no day of either sport is planned above the first report alone (0 of all comparisons), and none above the second report alone within its reduction; the only 2 differences, 6 and 20 days later, are a core row the plan's time budget keeps or drops (equal or lower doses on every shared row).
probes.P2 race rungs: Race on the race-week Saturday under each window intent: REST NO_SESSION; LIGHT_ACTIVITY_ONLY OPTIONAL_WALK 20; REDUCE_SUBSTANTIAL and REDUCE_LIGHT EASY_RUN 20; a Sunday race (not a run day) NO_SESSION; no strength on race day; the race-week touch runs easy (role EASY); offer once; no EVENT_AMBITIOUS item. Situation 2 restart with the race the next week: EASY_RUN 15, offer.

namedBlockers.definition: SSCTR-V1CPR-03 (+QRE-V1CPR-04): D49 on executed sets, on the rungs and in the first week after the ladder
evidence: Both directed tests pass (red at 5ee9dec), including the first week placed by the review (RED_D49_FIRST_WEEK).
P6: 4176 checks over 144 scenarios on the ladder and the first week after it, 0 above the last executed count plus one.

founderDecisions.evidence: No speed reaches the held doses because a window ended: P11b (180 cases) and P13; a missed or unreported session repeats the rung with no debt or regression; an unreviewed week repeats (NB-4); waited days are days without training with the R6 class bounds (P13, SSCTR-FF-N1). Checks come only at the window's end, at weekly reviews of affected weeks, after adverse sessions and when the athlete chooses an early end: no daily questionnaire. No watch, exam, certificate or physical test is a condition of any return.
exceptions: SSCTR-FFR-01 (NB-4 residual): a progression by calendar after an off-review check.
SSCTR-FFR-02 (NB-1 residual): days without training across a chain are dropped, so a return reads a shorter stop than the record shows.

SSCTR-FFR-06 (introduced on the NB-3 path): a question loop keeps the reviews of the return's first weeks from deciding and refuses a 'not 100%' report, which is neither a low-friction return nor executed sessions deciding.
SSCTR-FFR-03 (minor, decision precision): FASTER's R4 shortcut after waited days.

founderDecisions.evidence: P11b: the three speeds differ in every row swept; FASTER equals BALANCED only where FF-Q1 says (REDUCE_LIGHT with no whole executed week, disclosed 'one easier week first at both'); CONSERVATIVE never faster than BALANCED; the speed choice is never evidence (the execution read is speed-independent, C-FF1-2). Speeds stay separate from the coach profiles (P12). Never artificially aggressive: FASTER's shortcut needs a whole executed and checked week (SSCTR-FFR-03 refines it after waited days).

The race keeps its role, id and date and is flagged as the athlete's own event with the coach's recommendation for that day; in scope it is never prescribed at race effort or as a completion and never automatically adequate; no race question blocks and eligible training is never held for a race answer; the three paths are offered once with keep as the default; keeping the date never ends or shortens a reduction or a return; leaving the scope is disclosed; no pre-race held start passes the race; the Situation 2 restart is in scope; the date-change route applies the same rule (P2, P9, P16; directed tests).

P10 and the FF-Q3 directed test: the short check ends the reduction from the day after the report, with today's screen (missing: ASK); a warning sign or a clinical flag routes clinical; no clinical recovery is presumed (copy says 'passed or clearly improved', never recovered or cleared); a restriction and a held sport in force are unchanged; the early end does not reset the 14-day count; the speeds read the days the window lasted (a 1- or 2-day window takes the up-to-10-days rows; a mid-week first week repeats).

P12 and the FF-Q4 test: DEMANDING prescribes exactly what BALANCED prescribes across generation, reviews and F08 paths; its only differences are P4's ACCEPT advice and the COACH_DEMANDING disclosure, which says the doses and limits are the balanced coach's. The integration contract (section 10.5) says it must not be presented as distinct prescriptive behaviour.

newFindings.title: An off-review check makes an unexecuted ladder week count as checked, so the ladder steps by calendar
newFindings.location: CoachingCore/src/r6-adaptation.mjs missedLadderWeek (a check of kind RETURN or WINDOW_END dated in the week or the Monday after marks the week checked, whatever was executed); episodeLadder evaluates execution only at the weekly review of the current week
newFindings.scenario: HYBRID with known dumbbell rows (4 sets). NEED_REST REST 5 days from week-1 Tuesday, returnSpeed FASTER; WELLBEING_CHECK on week-1 Sunday, improved: return R3 (week 2), R4 (week 3). No session of week 2 executed and no weekly review of week 2; a WELLBEING_CHECK on week-2 Saturday with every warning sign no (KEEP 'your return continues with what you execute'). The week-3 Monday review: KEEP, week 3 stays R4 at the held doses (bench and row 3x8 at RIR 3, long 45). Without the Saturday check the same review repeats R3 (1-2 sets at RIR 4, long 35). BALANCED variant (REDUCE_SUBSTANTIAL 5 days, R2/R3/R4, R2 week not executed, Saturday check): week 3 R3, week 4 R4, R2 skipped. 5ee9dec gives the same result for the off-review variant.
newFindings.expected: returnLadder.transitionRule and D1: a rung is left only after a whole plan week at it with every prescribed session executed and no adverse or conflicting response, with its check; an elapsed week that no review evaluated and whose sessions were not all executed counts as not executed; its rung repeats with no debt.
newFindings.minimalCorrection: In missedLadderWeek, per sport, a week with a check is skipped only when its prescribed sessions of that sport were all executed with no adverse or conflicting response (executionOf(...).all), or when its weekly review already recorded its repeat (repeatOf); otherwise it counts as missed. No new number. Directed test: the scenario above, red on 4630bca.
newFindings.owner: Engineering (one narrow fix cycle if the Chief opens it), then a narrow SSCTR recheck

newFindings.classification: BLOCKING (residual of NB-1, CH-r2-7 read with SSCTR-FF-N1)
newFindings.title: After a chained rest report, the return reads only the last contiguous window: rest days of an earlier window of the same chain, and return days with no executed session, are dropped
newFindings.location: CoachingCore/src/r6-adaptation.mjs sportPlan (the backward scan stops at the first day not held by a WINDOW or WAIT marker of the chain)
newFindings.scenario: HYBRID with known rows. NEED_REST REST 7 days from week-1 Monday (11-16..11-22), FASTER; week-2 Monday 06:00 WELLBEING_CHECK improved: return from 11-23. The Monday strength and Tuesday run of the return are not executed. Thursday 11-26: UNUSUAL_FATIGUE REST (the 14-day count allows 4 days). Week-3 Monday check improved: plans RUN and STRENGTH 'REST row, 4 days': FASTER R3, R4 (easy 35, long 55 the next week; strength 1-2 sets then 2-3), BALANCED R2, R3, R4. Days without any executed session: 14 (11-16..11-29). The same 14 days as one REST window give the MODERATE recipe (15-min runs, 20-min long, 1 set at RIR 4; BALANCED holds the first step). With 6 waited days before the check: 20 days without training, read as 10, FASTER R3, R4. When the two return sessions were executed, the 4-day reading is right and is unchanged.
newFindings.expected: CH-r2-7: the REST/LIGHT rows read the sport's R0/R1 days plus its waited days across its chain's windows (here at least 11, the MODERATE class); SSCTR-FF-N1: days without training are days without training; C-Q05-5: planned sessions all missed read as rest. A combination is never less conservative than the record of days without training.
newFindings.minimalCorrection: In sportPlan, per sport, continue the backward scan through the chain's earlier windows and waits, reading as rest any stretch of the chain's own return in which no prescribed session of that sport was executed, and stop at the sport's last executed session; the row then reads those days with the existing R6 class bounds. No new number. Directed tests: the scenario (14 days: MODERATE at every speed with its holds; 20 days with the wait: MODERATE), and the executed variant unchanged.
newFindings.owner: Engineering (same narrow cycle), then a narrow SSCTR recheck

newFindings.classification: NON_BLOCKING (decision precision; the candidate conforms to SSCTR-FF-N1 (b) as written)
newFindings.title: FASTER's R4 shortcut after REDUCE_LIGHT survives up to 10 waited days without training
newFindings.scenario: REDUCE_LIGHT 10 days from week-1 Monday, FASTER, week 1 executed and reviewed with its check, days 8-10 executed; the check comes 6 or 10 days after the window's end (no training meanwhile): the plan is R4 (bench and row 4x8 at RIR 3, long 55) where the last completed week was 3x8 at RIR 4 with a 45-min long run. The R6 SHORT class for those waited days resumes the last completed doses with no step until execution, so N1 (b)'s premise ('never less conservative than the R6 SHORT resume') fails for the shortcut.
newFindings.minimalCorrection: FASTER goes straight to R4 only when the check comes with no waited day (on or before the day after the window's end); with any waited day FASTER is R3, R4 (equal to BALANCED, disclosed). No new number.
newFindings.owner: Chief: next eligible change; SSCTR re-review of FF-Q1 x N1

newFindings.title: A declared break's return reviewed in a week a superseded Situation 1 wait emptied starts next week, and the week keeps 'waiting for your check' with no check possible
newFindings.scenario: NEED_REST REST 7 days from week-4 Monday, no check; TRAVEL break 12-14..12-20 reported Monday 12-21 07:00: the wait markers end, but returnAfterPause counts the emptied sessions as not ahead (fromWeek = next week), adds RETURN_WAIT, and week 6 has no session, each saying 'Waiting for your check'; a WELLBEING_CHECK then answers 'nothing to check'. The same 14-day break alone starts the MODERATE return on 12-21.
newFindings.minimalCorrection: When the declared break's return supersedes a wait, count the sessions the wait emptied this week as ahead for the re-entry week, and never leave the wait's text on a session no check can release. No new number.

newFindings.title: A ladder week with no prescribed strength session (race or taper week) is read as 'not done as planned' for strength
newFindings.scenario: Race week inside an R3 ladder with both strength slots REST_BY_DESIGN: the review says 'strength: this week was not done as planned, so its step repeats next week' (also journey F). SSCTR-FF-Q2 (d): a week in which a sport has only optional sessions is not a ladder week for that sport. The rung reaches the next week either way.
newFindings.minimalCorrection: Carry the rung to the next week without the repeat wording when the sport had no prescribed session that week.

newFindings.classification: BLOCKING (introduced by the NB-3 fix; a question loop on the NB-3 path)
newFindings.title: After a single declared break read per sport (NB-3), every later review of the return's first weeks asks to confirm the interruption again, and confirming it does not end the question
newFindings.location: CoachingCore/src/r6-adaptation.mjs staleReturn (recomputes the entry with the interruption's own class r.cls from breakOf, while the return recorded the per-sport entry of classBySport and stopBySport); called for every review kind except a return or a readiness declaration (evaluateProgram, decide)
newFindings.scenario: HYBRID with known rows. NEED_REST REST 7 days from week-4 Monday (12-07..12-13), no check; TRAVEL break 12-14..12-20 reported Monday 12-21: REESTABLISH, per sport MODERATE from 12-07 (correct, NB-3). Then a WELLBEING_CHECK, a 'not 100%' report (UNUSUAL_FATIGUE REDUCE_SUBSTANTIAL) and the weekly reviews of weeks 6 and 7 (week 7 executed) all return ASK 'Training before the interruption that began on 2026-12-14 is now recorded, and the return reported on 2026-12-21 did not read it: confirm that interruption again ... nothing else changes until then'. Confirming it (RETURN_AFTER_PAUSE with its episodeId) re-plans, and the next review asks again. On a 12-week program the loop stops only in week 8 (once the review week passes the return's fromWeek). On 5ee9dec the same steps give KEEP.
newFindings.expected: A recorded return is stale only when the record changed what it read. The athlete's reports and reviews are decided (D1: executed sessions decide; Situation 1 stays available, DR-148 (2)); no question is asked endlessly (the principle D3 states for races and SSCTR-V1CPR-02 applied to dead ends).
newFindings.minimalCorrection: In staleReturn, recompute each sport's entry with the class and stop the return recorded for that sport (classBySport, stopBySport), as returnAfterPause composed it. No new number. Directed test: the scenario above (a weekly review, a check and a report after the NB-3 return are decided; confirming is never needed), red on 4630bca.
newFindings.owner: Engineering (same narrow cycle), then a narrow recheck

dispositionRationale: NB-2, NB-3 (its own defect), NB-5 and NB-6 are closed, D2, D3, D4 and D6 are implemented as sporting rules, and the default path is unchanged. Three MAJOR, narrow, runtime-only defects remain. Two are residuals of named blockers' own defect class: NB-4 (SSCTR-FFR-01, a calendar step to the held doses after an off-review check) and NB-1 (SSCTR-FFR-02, CH-r2-7 drops days without training across a chain). The third, SSCTR-FFR-06, was introduced by the NB-3 fix: a question loop that keeps the reviews and reports of the return's first weeks from being decided. All three fit the single narrow, runtime-only fix cycle the bounded-cycle rule allows, with a narrow recheck of those paths (and of CF-OBS-1 if included).

aeReview.question: Is the current plan still adequate?
aeReview.answer: For the paths verified, yes: the candidate plans what the decided rules require. In the two residual paths it plans above the evidence the record holds.

aeReview.question: Is there a sufficient material fact, with provenance?
aeReview.answer: Reports, checks and executed sessions on the record. An off-review check is a fact about signs, not about a week's execution (SSCTR-FFR-01); the record does show the days without training that SSCTR-FFR-02 drops.

aeReview.question: Is KEEP defensible, and what is unknown?
aeReview.answer: KEEP of the candidate is not defensible for the two residuals and the loop; everything else may stand. Unknown: individual response, as in the decision.

aeReview.question: Is change really necessary, relative to a comparator?
aeReview.answer: Yes: the comparators are the transitionRule (NB-4), the R6 classes through SSCTR-FF-N1 and CH-r2-7 (NB-1), and, for SSCTR-FFR-06, the decided reviews of 5ee9dec on the same steps.

aeReview.question: What is the smallest sufficient intervention?
aeReview.answer: Three runtime corrections, in missedLadderWeek, sportPlan and staleReturn, with directed tests; no new number.

aeReview.question: Why are relevant smaller alternatives insufficient?
aeReview.answer: Copy cannot stop a dose planned without evidence; a client rule (no off-review checks) would leave the record unable to decide; a disclosure would still plan the dose.

aeReview.question: Does the trade-off protect the stated priority and progression?
aeReview.answer: Yes: both only remove a step the evidence does not support; executed weeks still progress at the chosen speed.

aeReview.question: Does applicable evidence support the conclusion and dose?
aeReview.answer: The conclusions apply decided rules (transitionRule, CH-r2-7, SSCTR-FF-N1, R6 classes; S06's graded return as the decision's context, CL-1). No dose is added.

aeReview.question: What material uncertainty remains?
aeReview.answer: The combination logic and the class bounds are internal and unvalidated; recurrence across regions (O-1); urgency wording (G04).

aeReview.question: Is ASK, HOLD or CLINICAL_HUMAN_REQUIRED needed?
aeReview.answer: No clinical item is raised by this record. CF-OBS-1 is a gap in enforcing an existing clinical hold, routed to Security, QRE and Engineering.
